clue.text: It's very easy to upset

parts.note: read literally, something easy to knock down or tip off its feet; idiomatically, someone easily beaten or persuaded

explanation.surface: A remark about a touchy person who takes offence at the slightest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' suggests hurt feelings, but here it means physically knocked over, which is the literal sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy victory or a gullible person is idiomatically something you can knock over with no effort.

clue.text: Ostentation is forbidden in 17

indicators.note: something forbidden is kept out, so the word is barred from the longer word

parts.note: refers to the answer at 17 down, the garden of Eden

explanation.surface: Showing off is banned in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forbidden in' removes IS from PARADISE (17 down), leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a parade of something is to show it off, so the noun is a synonym for display or ostentation.

clue.text: A constant wind is present throughout this flight

definitions.text: A constant wind is present throughout this flight

parts.words: A constant wind is present throughout this flight
parts.note: the wind is a winding or twisting, not moving air, and the flight is a flight of steps, not a plane journey

explanation.surface: A passenger complaining of steady gusts all through an aeroplane journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' (rhymes with 'kind') means a turn, and 'flight' is a set of stairs; the surface wants weather and aviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase that keeps turning round a central column is constantly winding along its whole flight of steps.

clue.text: Veteran soldier keeps in hiding

indicators.note: the word soldier holds the answer concealed within its letters

explanation.surface: An old soldier who stays out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for an old person or old thing, an old-timer or veteran.

clue.text: Non-7 sort of triangle with one side too many!

definitions.text: Non-7 sort of triangle with one side too many!

parts.words: Non-7 sort of triangle with one side too many!
parts.note: a triangle that is not mathematical (7 down) but romantic: three people in a love affair, one of them surplus

explanation.surface: A geometry joke about a triangle with an extra side.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 down is the answer TRIGONOMETRICAL; the clue's triangle is the classic love triangle, where the third party is the side too many.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the eternal triangle' names a romantic entanglement among three people, typically two rivals for one lover.

clue.text: Floods in spring set to return

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: returning means the word set is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A forecast of floods expected again in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reads the word set backwards; 'spring' suggests the season but is a mineral spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers in spate are in flood, so spates are sudden floods or rushes of water.

clue.text: Incurable optimist needs only a plan to work out

indicators.note: the letters must be worked out into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who is hopeful as long as they have a plan to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work out' rearranges ONLY A PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the relentlessly cheerful heroine of Eleanor Porter's novel, the name now means an irrepressible optimist.

clue.text: Motoring article possibly about angular functions

indicators.note: signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece in a car magazine that might discuss the angles of a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MOTORING ARTICLE; the definition is adjectival, 'about' meaning 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine, cosine and tangent are angular functions, the subject matter of this branch of mathematics.

clue.text: Pete's act is painful to watch

indicators.note: a painful act is a mess, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of Pete's without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre review saying Pete's performance is excruciating to sit through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painful' rearranges PETES ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To look on as a spectator at an event is to watch it.

clue.text: Dancer, for example, in team of eight

definitions.text: Dancer, for example, in team of eight

parts.words: Dancer, for example, in team of eight
parts.note: Dancer is one of Santa's sleigh team of eight named animals, not a performer in a dance troupe

explanation.surface: A dancer who belongs to an eight-person troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancer, Prancer, Vixen and the rest pull Santa's sleigh in the Christmas poem; the capital D is a name, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The animals pulling Santa Claus's sleigh are this Arctic deer, eight of them in the traditional poem.

clue.text: Position Crux occupies as a swimmer

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, filling it

parts.note: a place is a position
the setter refers to themself, so I

explanation.surface: The setter claims a spot as a swimmer in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Crux is the setter's pseudonym, so it stands for I; 'occupies' puts I inside PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer is crossword shorthand for a fish, and this flatfish is one.

clue.text: Progress slowly like leaderless bird

indicators.note: the word loses its leading, first letter

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A rare bird, lacking a flock leader, edges forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To move forward a small distance at a time, like an inchworm, is to progress slowly.

clue.text: Duke, playboy, and world traveller

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker

explanation.surface: A list describing a jet-setting aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was the first Englishman to sail round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake circumnavigated the globe in the Golden Hind, making him a famous world traveller.

clue.text: She would choose best butter, no doubt

definitions.text: She would choose best butter, no doubt

parts.words: She would choose best butter, no doubt
parts.note: a butter here is something that butts with its head; she is a female animal that butts

explanation.surface: A fussy housewife or childminder who insists on the finest dairy butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is one who butts, and 'nanny' suggests a childminder doing the shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A female goat is a well-known butter, charging with its horns, and as a goat it would pick the best one.

clue.text: Also a balloon

parts.note: to balloon is to swell up

explanation.surface: A child adding that they'd like a balloon too.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition or too, a synonym for also.

clue.text: Rules once negotiated for the pound

indicators.note: terms that are negotiated get reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Old currency rules that were once agreed for sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges RULES ONCE; 'pound' is not money but a pen for stray animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound in which stray animals are kept is a fenced area, an enclosure.

clue.text: Gift for the poor — a welcome gesture

definitions.meaning: charity given to the needy, such as money or food
a hand held out to greet someone

explanation.definitionFit: Charity distributed free to the needy is one sense; split as two words, a hand stretched out in greeting is the other.

clue.text: Soldier dies at sea, hoping for this perhaps

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: something at sea is confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier dying in a sea battle, perhaps hoping for heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' jumbles the word dies; the definition leans on the whole clue, a dying soldier hoping for heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven, the afterlife a dying soldier might hope to reach, is the realm of eternal bliss.

clue.text: Bend in any direction? The very opposite!

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
an arch is a bend or curve

explanation.surface: Advice to flex in all directions, followed by a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bend in any direction' reads as a stretching instruction; split after 'any', and the remainder defines by opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless disorder is the opposite of direction or control, so the definition works by contrast.

clue.text: Fine given to the old is a burden

indicators.note: one piece is handed into the other, placed inside it

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of 'the', as in 'ye olde'
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A penalty imposed on an elderly person proves hard to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoke is figuratively an oppressive load or burden, like the wooden bar on oxen.

clue.text: Superior channel swimmer loses heart

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Leander swam the Hellespont, a sea channel, nightly to see Hero

explanation.surface: An elite cross-Channel swimmer runs out of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander of Greek myth swam the Hellespont, not the English Channel; drop his middle N.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior is a person in charge, someone above you, much as a leader is.

clue.text: Flower girl restricts the supply

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name that is also a flower
taken as written

explanation.surface: A florist's assistant rations out the stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is the adverb of supple, not the noun; 'restricts' means the flower girl's name holds the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply, read as the adverb from supple, means in a flexible, lissom way.

clue.text: Mature male first changes sex, paradoxically

indicators.note: the opening letter switches from F for female to M for male, odd since the word already means a man

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A grown man who undergoes a sex change at first, in a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: F is female and M male, so FELLOW's initial switching F to M is a 'sex change', paradoxical as a fellow is already male.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellow means mature and softened by age, as in mellow wine or a mellow temperament.

clue.text: Pilots may be badly let down by it

definitions.text: Pilots may be badly let down by it

parts.words: Pilots may be badly let down by it
parts.note: let down means literally dropped in altitude, not disappointed

explanation.surface: A complaint that airmen are often disappointed by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let down' sounds like disappointment but means a sudden drop in the aircraft's height.
explanation.definitionFit: A region of turbulent downdraught makes an aircraft suddenly lose height, dropping the plane and pilot.

clue.text: Not quite a colour match

indicators.note: the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: green is a colour

explanation.surface: A paint sample that doesn't quite match the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that match correspond with each other, which is to agree.

clue.text: Dusty room, a dry one, and cold

parts.note: TT means teetotal, i.e. dry
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A description of an unheated, parched room collecting dust.
explanation.definitionFit: The loft under the roof is the classic dusty room where things are stored and forgotten.

clue.text: Flight pioneer from the Arctic — a Russian

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: An early aviator who came from the far north of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek mythical figure flew on wax wings that melted near the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he flew with feathered wings made by his father Daedalus, an early pioneer of flight.

clue.text: Not laid down by Article V, possibly

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal ruling not established by a particular clause of a constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid down' suggests legislation, but it means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upright stands rather than lies flat, so it is not laid down horizontally.

clue.text: Sporting side appearing in Mexico

parts.note: the Roman numeral for the number of players sits in the middle of the word Mexico

explanation.surface: A national team competing in a Mexican tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters X and I in the middle of 'Mexico' make the Roman numeral XI.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team has that many players, so a team is called by the number.

clue.text: State of 18 in which many may suffer suspension

definitions.text: State of 18 in which many may suffer suspension

parts.words: State of 18 in which many may suffer suspension
parts.note: 18 is lawlessness; suspension means hanging by mob justice, not a temporary ban

explanation.surface: A state in turmoil where many people get suspended from work or school.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is ANARCHY; 'suspension' means hanging from a rope rather than being barred from duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Summary execution by a mob without trial, often by hanging, is rough justice that flourishes amid lawlessness.
